title: Collector Training Q&A: Client Charity-Care and Insurance Credits in Two-Payment Settlement Pricing
content:
# Two-Payment Settlement — Client Credit Reductions

**The rule taught.** In pricing a Two-Payment Settlement offer under Ridgeline's Settlement Agreements, where the client has booked a charity-care write-off credit to the account, the Two-Payment assistance reduction of 2.0 points applies; where the client has booked an insurance payment credit to the account and no charity-care write-off, the Two-Payment adjudicated-balance reduction of 1.0 point applies; an account with neither credit carries no credit reduction for a Two-Payment offer.

The credits are the client credits shown in the money history of the Placed Consumer Accounts record: a client adjustment booked as a charity-care write-off, or a client adjustment booked as an insurance payment.

## Questions and answers

**Q. The account's history shows both a charity-care write-off credit and an insurance payment credit. Which reduction applies?**
A. The assistance reduction of 2.0 points. The adjudicated-balance reduction of 1.0 point applies only where there is an insurance payment credit and no charity-care write-off.

**Q. The history shows two insurance payment credits and no charity-care write-off. Is the reduction doubled?**
A. No. The adjudicated-balance reduction is 1.0 point whether one or several insurance payment credits are booked.

**Q. The consumer says the hospital wrote part of the bill off, but the account's history shows no client credit of either kind. What applies?**
A. No credit reduction. The rule turns on the credits the client has booked to the account.

## Summary grid

| Charity-care write-off credit booked | Insurance payment credit booked | Reduction |
|---|---|---|
| yes | yes or no | 2.0 percentage points |
| no | yes | 1.0 percentage point |
| no | no | none |
